overall_reason: The hero exploded-axonometric diagram keeps five equal layers, one accent on the layer that matters ('Type reference'), one leader-line grammar and labels outside the drawing, and the gallery shows the same one-accent system across its specimens.

score.reason: T-DIAGRAM-FOCAL, T-CONNECTORS and T-GRAYSCALE pass on the hero diagram; the gallery's radar specimen carries four filled series (DVZ-120) and T-CHART-375 could not be run.

findings.where: gallery card 'Radar', button.pl:nth-of-type(11) > picture > img (radar.webp, 355 by 222px), 1440, contact sheet #9, tiles/1440-05.png
findings.evidence: The radar specimen overlays four filled polygons (MinIO, Amazon S3, Ceph, Google Cloud Storage per its alt text) on five axes; on the crop the three grey fills overlap into one shape and only the orange one stands apart.
findings.before: A four-series filled radar as the template for 'multiple entities scored'.
findings.after: Show two or three series as outlines with the focal one filled, or use a small table or dot plot for four products on five criteria.
findings.why: Past three filled series a radar hides the shapes it exists to compare, and because the gallery is the skill's own output, the specimen teaches that form.

findings.evidence: The line-chart specimen puts a marker on every point of the accent series (about 8 dots on one line) over an area fill.
findings.before: Markers on every point plus an area fill.
findings.after: Drop the markers except the last point and any point the caption names.
findings.why: Markers on every point add ink without adding information and compete with the line's shape.

strengths: The hero diagram (contact #1, 534 by 465px) has five same-size layers, one orange accent on 'Type reference', a title and a description in the svg ('From a sentence to a finished diagram'), and a figure caption; it reads in 30 seconds from 'Your prompt' at the base to 'HTML + SVG' at the top.
Its leader lines are straight horizontals from each layer to a label outside the drawing (no crossings, none through nodes), and the dashed verticals mean one thing: the stacking axis.

Each gallery image has alt text that states what the diagram shows ('Polar chart of request demand across eight UTC windows on a 0 to 100 percent scale').
